plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: it guarantees winning whenever the second-highest bid is below my value and never causes overpayment because the price is the second-highest bid. With value $31 and no future-round strategic considerations, bidding 31 maximizes expected profit and avoids leaving positive-surplus wins on the table or risking negative surplus. ]

In a sealed-bid second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ bids. There's only one round, so no strategic signaling. My private value is 22; I should bid 22 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 22 and pay that second-highest bid. Any higher or lower bid could only reduce expected payoff or risk losing profitable wins. Therefore, bid 22.

Second-price auction with i.i.d. private values: truthful bidding is dominant. With value 40 and no history to exploit in this single round, bidding my true value maximizes expected profit. Underbidding risks losing when it would be profitable; overbidding risks winning at prices above my value. Therefore, bid exactly 40.
